title: Gentle token-backpressure: token-wallet admission with staged-response fallbacks
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce a client-scoped "token-wallet" admission mechanism that provides gentle, configurable backpressure by spending budgeted credits to accept full-fidelity requests and falling back to staged lower-fidelity responses when budgets are exhausted. The wallet is decoupled from hard rejects: instead of dropping requests outright during regional congestion, the admission controller consults the token-wallet and chooses between full response, degraded response (model/quantization downgrade, shorter max tokens, or synthesized partial response), or soft-hold (deferred execution). This ticket covers design, prototype, metrics, rollout, and runbook for integration with existing priority lanes and circuit-breaker thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: A stable token-wallet API that allows per-tenant budgeting and per-route spend rules
Admission controller consults wallet and reliably chooses: ACCEPT_FULL / ACCEPT_DEGRADED / DEFER / REJECT based on policy
Degraded response modes implemented: model-quantize (lower-precision), max-token-trim, and heuristic partial-synthesis; each mode is selectable per route
Integration tests that simulate region-level saturation and demonstrate >40% reduction in outright rejections for medium and high-priority tenants
Dashboards with wallet balances, spend rate, degrade-rate, P95 latency, and SLO error budget burn for the canary cohort
Canary rollout plan documented and rollback hooks implemented in the admission controller
implementation_notes: Wallet model: per-tenant rolling budget (tokens/minute) + burstable reserve. Default budget 1000 credits/min, configurable by plan.
Cost mapping: define credit cost per operation (base request cost + per-output-token multiplier). Different routes map to different cost tables.

Decision flow: 1) fast-path: if wallet >= full_cost -> ACCEPT_FULL; 2) else if wallet >= degraded_cost -> ACCEPT_DEGRADED; 3) else if deferable(route) and queue_depth < threshold -> DEFER (soft-hold); 4) else REJECT/trigger CB.
Priority lanes: token-wallet interacts with high/med/low priority queues. High-priority tenants have higher budgets and lower degrade thresholds.

Circuit breaker integration: if region error rate or latency crosses CB threshold we progressively lower degraded_cost and widen fallback modes; if wallet spend spikes correlate with cross-region failover, throttle wallet rewrites to avoid oscillation.

Multi-region behavior: wallets are global per-tenant but locally cached in each region with lease-based sync to avoid cross-region bottlenecks. On primary-region saturation prefer degraded responses over automatic cross-region failover for non-critical tenants to conserve cross-region capacity and cost.
Backward compatibility: default policy for existing tenants is ACCEPT_FULL until wallet enforcement is enabled; feature flag gated per-account.
Observability: instrument accepting decisions and the selected fallback mode with tags: tenant_id, route, region, chosen_mode, wallet_balance_before, wallet_balance_after.
Data retention: wallet events retained 30d for troubleshooting; aggregate metrics retained 90d for SLO analysis.
testing_plan: Unit tests for cost accounting, decision logic, and wallet expiry semantics
E2E tests that simulate load profiles: steady, bursty, and noisy neighbours; assert acceptance/degrade/reject ratios
Chaos tests: kill primary region and assert wallets correctly cause degraded-mode preference vs immediate cross-region shift for controlled cohorts
Load tests to validate that soft-hold queueing reduces peak rejection by at least 30% under synthetic spikes
Regression tests against existing admission APIs to ensure no latency regression in the fast-path (<2ms median decision)
metrics_targets: Reduce outright REJECT rate under 99th-percentile spikes by >=30% for medium-priority tenants
Maintain P95 latency for ACCEPT_FULL paths within current SLO +/-5%
Accept_DEGRADED path latency target P95 < 2x ACCEPT_FULL P95
Wallet accounting accuracy: <0.1% drift across regional caches after 24h of churn
Canary SLO burn rate for affected cohort remains < 1.5x baseline during test window
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind rollout flag 'token_wallet_v1' at route and account scope
Stage 0 (lab): unit + e2e + chaos tests pass
Stage 1 (canary): enable for 1% of traffic across low-variability tenants for 72h, monitor metrics
Stage 2 (expanded canary): 5% traffic including some medium-priority tenants; synthetic spike tests during the window
Stage 3 (gradual): 25% then 50% with progressively stricter threshold tuning
Stage 4 (full): opt-in for accounts, then auto-enforce for pay-as-you-go accounts after 2 weeks of stable metrics
Rollback: immediately flip feature flag off, flush wallet caches and allow in-flight scaled-down requests to finish; run postmortem on any SLO violation
runbook: If REJECT rate spikes > 2x baseline: check wallet service pod errors, sync lag, and per-tenant balances
If circuit breaker trips in a region: increase degraded_cost to favor ACCEPT_DEGRADED for low/med tenants and trigger canary traffic to fallback region for high-tier only
Manual override: ops can set tenant wallet to unlimited for a short window via admin console for customers impacted by false positives
If wallet cache divergence detected (>1% mismatch): trigger full resync and fail open (temporarily accept_all) until resolved
Post-incident: capture example traces and wallet event history; correlate with model load, autoscaling events, and cross-region routing decisions
updates: 2026-02-02: Initial design spike completed. Prototype wallet implemented as in-memory sharded counters. Observed edge-case when bursts exceed cache TTL leading to temporary over-acceptance.
2026-02-12: Decided on lease-based cache sync (200ms lease + jitter) to limit cross-region contention. Tradeoff: small chance of over-accept during lease expiry vs reduced cross-region RPCs.
2026-02-20: Integration design session with console team: admin override UI and per-tenant budget controls approved. UX will be minimal for v1.
2026-02-25: PR #7234 opened for wallet service and admission controller hooks. Basic unit tests added. Status: needs load test harness.

2026-03-03: Load-testing: reduced peak rejects by 36% in simulated burst for medium-priority tenants, but observed 12% higher P95 on ACCEPT_DEGRADED paths. Decided to tune degraded-cost mapping and add a fast-path low-latency degraded mode (shorter tokens) to meet latency targets.
2026-03-08: Security review not required for v1 (no sensitive material in wallet), but privacy noted: retain only tenant IDs and counters; avoid storing prompts. Confirmed in design doc.
2026-03-12: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-20 to 1% traffic. Monitoring dashboards prepared and alert runbook drafted. Next: finalize E2E chaos tests and peer review feedback from infra team.
notes: Trade-offs considered: token-wallet vs hard token-bucket per request. Wallet is fairer across bursty tenants but slightly more complex for consistency.
Alternative considered: always prefer cross-region failover for overflow. Rejected due to cost and risk of cascading failovers across regions.
Future work: tie wallet budgets to billing/plan so customers can buy higher budgets; expose simulated wallet preview in Console for troubleshooting.
Owners: runtime-engineering (implementation), console (admin controls), observability (dashboards & alerts)
rollback_plan: Flip 'token_wallet_v1' feature flag off at route/account scope. If flip does not restore normal behavior within 5 minutes, run emergency config to accept_all on the admission controller for affected region and open incident. Post-rollback: collect diagnostics, wallet dump, and start hotfix cycle.
risk_assessment: Medium. Primary risk is wallet consistency across regions causing temporary unfairness or double-spend. Mitigations: lease-based caching, conservative defaults, canary rollout, and ability to fail-open. Secondary risk: degraded responses causing customer confusion; mitigations include clear indicators in Console and customer-facing docs for troubleshooting.
